units.title: Proportional Relationships
units.blurb: Recognize proportional relationships in tables, graphs and equations, and solve proportions.

units.title: Percent Problems
units.blurb: Solve percent problems about change, discounts, tax, interest and error.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting Signed Numbers
units.blurb: See adding as moving on a number line and subtracting as adding the opposite.

units.title: Multiplying and Dividing Signed Numbers
units.blurb: Learn why the sign rules work and convert fractions to decimals.

units.title: Expressions
units.blurb: Combine like terms, expand and factor linear expressions, and rewrite expressions to show meaning.

units.title: Equations and Inequalities
units.blurb: Solve two-step equations and inequalities, and use them to solve problems.

units.title: Angles, Circles and Solids
units.blurb: Use angle relationships, build triangles, work with circles, and find area, surface area and volume.

units.title: Sampling and Comparing Data
units.blurb: Use random samples to draw conclusions and compare two groups.

units.title: Probability
units.blurb: Measure chance from 0 to 1, compare models with experiments, and find probabilities of compound events.

topics.title: Unit Rates with Fractions
topics.short: Walking 1/2 mile in 1/4 hour is 2 miles per hour.
topics.trouble: Students divide the time by the distance and get hours per mile.

topics.title: Is It Proportional?
topics.short: Every ratio y/x in the table is the same.
topics.trouble: Students call any steadily increasing relationship proportional, even y = x + 3.

topics.title: Proportional Graphs
topics.short: A proportional graph is a straight line through the origin.
topics.trouble: Students accept any straight line as proportional, even one that misses (0, 0).

topics.title: The Constant of Proportionality
topics.short: k = y/x is the unit rate in every row.

topics.title: Writing y = kx
topics.short: Turn a table or story into an equation.
topics.trouble: Students compute x/y instead of y/x and write the reciprocal as k.

topics.title: What a Point on the Graph Means
topics.short: (1, k) shows the unit rate; (0, 0) means none of each.

topics.title: Solving Proportions
topics.short: Use unit rates, scale factors, or cross products, and know why each works.
topics.trouble: Students cross-multiply a relationship that is not proportional, or set up the ratios with mismatched units.

topics.title: Percent Increase and Decrease
topics.short: Divide the change by the original amount.
topics.trouble: Students divide the change by the new amount instead of the original.

topics.title: Markups, Discounts and Tax
topics.short: Find sale prices and totals with percents.
topics.trouble: Students add two discounts together, thinking 20% off then 10% off is 30% off.

topics.title: Simple Interest
topics.short: Interest = principal × rate × time.

topics.title: Percent Error
topics.short: Compare an estimate with the actual value as a percent.

topics.title: Scale Drawings
topics.short: Use a scale to find actual lengths and areas.
topics.trouble: Students scale an area by the same factor as the lengths, when it scales by the factor squared.

topics.title: Opposites Make Zero
topics.short: A number and its opposite add to 0.

topics.title: Adding Integers
topics.short: Move right for positive, left for negative.
topics.trouble: With different signs, students add the absolute values, so −7 + 3 comes out as −10.

topics.title: Subtracting Integers
topics.short: Subtracting a number is adding its opposite.
topics.trouble: Students compute 3 − (−5) as −2, treating subtracting a negative like subtracting a positive.

topics.title: Distance Between Two Numbers
topics.short: The distance from a to b is |a − b|.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Numbers
topics.short: Use the same rules for negative fractions and decimals.

topics.title: Multiplying Integers
topics.short: A negative times a negative is positive, and the pattern shows why.
topics.trouble: Students carry the multiplication rule into addition, saying −3 + −4 = 7 because "two negatives make a positive."

topics.title: Dividing Integers
topics.short: The sign rules for dividing match those for multiplying.

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Numbers
topics.short: Apply the sign rules to fractions and decimals.

topics.title: Terminating and Repeating Decimals
topics.short: Divide to change a fraction to a decimal that ends or repeats.
topics.trouble: Students stop dividing too early and write 2/3 as 0.6.

topics.title: All Four Operations with Signed Numbers
topics.short: Solve problems with all four operations on rational numbers.
topics.trouble: Students apply the wrong sign rule when operations are mixed, such as treating −2 − 3 as a product.

topics.title: Combining Like Terms
topics.short: Add terms with the same variable part: 3x + 5x = 8x.
topics.trouble: Students combine unlike terms, writing 3x + 2 = 5x, or x + x = x².

topics.title: Expanding and Factoring Linear Expressions
topics.short: Distribute and factor with negative and fractional coefficients.
topics.trouble: Students distribute a negative to the first term only, writing −(x − 4) = −x − 4.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Expressions
topics.short: Subtracting an expression subtracts every term in it.
topics.trouble: Students subtract only the first term of the second expression.

topics.title: Rewriting Expressions to See Meaning
topics.short: a + 0.05a = 1.05a shows a 5% increase.

topics.title: One-Step Equations with Signed Numbers
topics.short: Solve x − 4.5 = −2 and −2/3 x = 8.
topics.trouble: Students divide by the opposite of the coefficient or drop its sign.

topics.title: Two-Step Equations
topics.short: Undo adding or subtracting, then undo multiplying or dividing.
topics.trouble: Students divide before undoing the addition, and then divide only part of the equation.

topics.title: Equations Like p(x + q) = r
topics.short: Divide first, or distribute first; both work.
topics.trouble: Students distribute to the first term only, or add q before dividing.

topics.title: Word Problems with Two-Step Equations
topics.short: Write and solve an equation, then compare with an arithmetic solution.

topics.title: Two-Step Inequalities
topics.short: Solve like an equation, but reverse the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
topics.trouble: Students forget to reverse the inequality after dividing by a negative number.

topics.title: Multistep Problems with Rational Numbers
topics.short: Mix fractions, decimals and percents and check with an estimate.

topics.title: Complementary, Supplementary and Vertical Angles
topics.short: Use angle pairs to find unknown angles.
topics.trouble: Students mix up complementary (90°) and supplementary (180°).

topics.title: Finding Unknown Angles with Equations
topics.short: Write and solve an equation from an angle diagram.

topics.title: Which Triangles Can Exist?
topics.short: Three lengths make a triangle only if each pair adds to more than the third.
topics.trouble: Students think any three lengths make a triangle, or that two angles and a side always give a unique one.

topics.title: Circumference and Pi
topics.short: Every circle's circumference is π times its diameter.
topics.trouble: Students use the radius where the diameter belongs, or think π is exactly 3.14.

topics.title: Area of a Circle
topics.short: Rearrange slices into a near-rectangle: A = πr².
topics.trouble: Students mix up 2πr and πr², or square the diameter.

topics.title: Slicing Solids
topics.short: Name the shapes made by slicing prisms and pyramids.

topics.title: Area and Surface Area Problems
topics.short: Find areas and surface areas of composite figures.

topics.title: Volume of Prisms
topics.short: V = Bh for any prism, where B is the area of the base.
topics.trouble: Students use the area of the side face as B instead of the base that matches the height.

topics.title: Random Samples
topics.short: A random sample gives every member an equal chance to be chosen.
topics.trouble: Students trust a large but convenient sample, such as asking only their friends.

topics.title: Making Predictions from Samples
topics.short: Use a sample's proportion to estimate the population.
topics.trouble: Students expect every sample to give exactly the same result.

topics.title: Comparing Two Groups
topics.short: Compare centers relative to spread to judge how different groups are.
topics.trouble: Students call two groups different whenever their means differ, ignoring how much the data overlap.

topics.title: Probability from 0 to 1
topics.short: 0 is impossible, 1 is certain, 1/2 is as likely as not.

topics.title: Theoretical Probability
topics.short: Equally likely outcomes: favorable over total.
topics.trouble: Students think any event with two outcomes, like winning the lottery, has probability 1/2.

topics.title: Experimental Probability
topics.short: Use relative frequency from trials to estimate probability.
topics.trouble: Students expect 60 rolls of a die to give exactly ten 6s.

topics.title: Comparing Models with Experiments
topics.short: Decide whether a model fits observed results.

topics.title: Sample Spaces with Lists, Tables and Trees
topics.short: List every outcome of a compound event.
topics.trouble: Students list "one head, one tail" once, missing that HT and TH are different outcomes.

topics.title: Probability of Compound Events
topics.short: Find a compound probability as a fraction of the sample space.
topics.trouble: Students add the probabilities of two independent events when they should multiply them.

topics.title: Simulating Chance Events
topics.short: Use random tools to estimate hard probabilities.
